# AdCP 3.3.0

**AdCP 3.3 is generally available.** The release artifact is `3.3.0` and the wire pin is `adcp_version: "3.3"`. 3.2 stays supported for integrations pinned to `"3.2"`, and nothing forces you to migrate. 3.3 is the last planned 3.x minor; the next feature release is 4.0.

3.3 brings the rest of media into the same buy as programmatic. A booking that waits on a traffic log, a host read, or a person's sign-off can say when it will be confirmed. A linear TV, print, or DOOH seller can report what it actually knows. And the places where two conformant 3.2 implementations could still disagree are settled.

- **What's new:** https://docs.adcontextprotocol.org/docs/reference/whats-new-in-3-3
- **Migrating from 3.2:** https://docs.adcontextprotocol.org/docs/reference/migration/3-2-to-3-3
- **Release notes:** https://docs.adcontextprotocol.org/docs/reference/release-notes#version-3-3-0
- **If you pinned a beta or RC:** https://docs.adcontextprotocol.org/docs/reference/3-3-beta

## Highlights

- **Scheduled and human-gated buying.** `expected_confirmation_at` on submitted buys and finalized proposals; holds you can plan, rank, and extend; vendor-metric outcome goals; governance budget periods; installment `change_cutoff`.
- **Delivery data offline sellers actually have.** Spot lifecycle and makegoods, print proof of insertion and circulation, structured DOOH location and impression basis, property-grain rollups, rows without impressions, and audience sizes as ranges.
- **Schemas open by default.** 744 of the 859 closed locations open, so a minor only adds and an older validator stops rejecting a newer peer for fields it does not know. Generated types change.
- **Fewer ways to disagree.** An account is its `account_id`. One agent-resolution rule covers every signing surface. Every task response carries the protocol envelope. Responses conform to the release the seller served. Discovery never provisions an account.
- **Agents that introduce themselves (experimental).** The Web Bot Auth signing profile, `trust.json`, demand-side grants, and seller onboarding posture let a buyer agent onboard with a seller it has never spoken to.
- **Proposals and offers (experimental).** Open opportunities with later proposals and `list_proposals`, and seller offers against an accepted buy. Signed terms bind every member, and a stale terms digest gets `PROPOSAL_TERMS_CHANGED`.

| Published surface | 3.2.1 | 3.3.0 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Manifested tools | 78 | 83 |
| Specialisms | 31 | 32 (`sales-fixed-rate`) |
| Standard error codes | 120 | 126 |

## Before you advertise `"3.3"`

3.3 removes no stable field, enum value, or task, but some rules narrow what a conformant implementation may do. Read [Required to claim 3.3 behavior](https://docs.adcontextprotocol.org/docs/reference/migration/3-2-to-3-3#required-to-claim-3-3-behavior) first. The ones with the widest reach: discovery never provisions an account, `account_id` is returned and accepted everywhere, signatures resolve agents by one rule (some that verified under 3.2 now fail), A2A hardening is MUST, `reporting_webhook.operation_id` fails closed, and seller revisions advance on every committed change.

## Withdrawn from 3.3, planned for 4.0

Definition pins, purchase rights, installment selection on the purchase, selection-dependent `price_adjustments`, `counting_mechanisms`, `target_audiences`, and `metric_id` on performance standards shipped in a 3.3 beta or release candidate and are not part of 3.3.0. Each extends the commercial terms, which are held closed until 4.0. The designs are kept in [Preparing for 4.0](https://docs.adcontextprotocol.org/docs/reference/migration/v4-compatibility#planned-for-4-0-withdrawn-from-3-3).

## Deprecations

All keep working throughout 3.x and are expected to be removed in 4.0: `seller_id` on event source and audience results, the natural-key account reference after provisioning and the account identity-rekey machinery, `principal_kind`, the RFC 9421 signing profiles, the boolean form of `demographics`, six reserved-word enum values, and the single-value form of the scalar-or-list unions (the `brand.json` color values stay until 5.0).

## SDKs

- **TypeScript:** `@adcp/sdk@17.0.0` ships alongside this release and embeds it (npm `latest` and `adcp-3.3`). `adcp-3.2` stays on 16.7.x.
- **Python:** `adcp==10.0.0` embeds this release and can follow it by a few days. Until it is on PyPI, keep Python integrations on `adcp` 9.x and `"3.2"`.
- **Go and Java:** no 3.3 support. Use raw-wire calls against the signed bundle.

## Support

| Line | Support |
|---|---|
| 3.3.x | Full support, for at least 12 months after 4.0 GA |
| 3.2.x | Security and critical fixes only |
| 3.1.x and 3.0.x | Security fixes only |

## Verify this release

The release carries the signed protocol tarball `3.3.0.tgz` with its `.sha256`, `.sig`, and `.crt`. Verify the Sigstore signature before using it as a build input: https://docs.adcontextprotocol.org/docs/reference/verifying-protocol-tarballs

The per-PR record is the `3.3.0` entry in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/adcontextprotocol/adcp/blob/v3.3.0/CHANGELOG.md).
